result_summary: The estimation pool controls the CMR gain as the mechanism predicts, but there is no crossover on the E01 eleven-summary fixture: d' rises strictly monotonically from 5.020 at pool 2 to 7.161 at pool 11 and no pool-size mean touches the 4.613 naive baseline, which is the pre-registered alternative branch. Spearman between the fitted direction's cosine to the 11-doc reference and the d' gain is 1.000 across the six pool sizes (0.884 across all 48 draws), clearing the 0.80 bar, with the cosine reading 0.8664 at pool 2 and 0.9834 at pool 8 exactly as predicted. V stays 0/24 at every pool size including the degenerate pool-2 per-pair arm, so the E09-H53 hurt endpoint (d' down, one violation) does not reproduce here and the E01/E09 discrepancy is a fixture term, not a pool-size term. Deliverable: the measured minimum estimation pool is 8 documents, about 71 pooled statements, the smallest pool whose direction reaches |cos| >= 0.98 of the full-pool reference while retaining 93.3% of the full-pool d'.
caveats: The harness reproduces E01 to within 0.05 closeness points and 0.02 in d', not bit-identically: E01 was measured on GPU bf16 and the GPUs are held by foreign jobs, so torch CPU fp32 is the reproduction path. The shipped OpenVINO INT8 encoder reads a little wider (+4.71 baseline margin, +19.41 full pool, d' 4.684 / 7.310) and changes no conclusion. Pool sizes 2 and 11 are deterministic by construction, so only four of the six points carry real error bars; the pool-3 spread is wide enough (+-0.647) that one draw of 48 lands at 4.566, 0.048 below baseline, while the pool-3 mean stays 1.29 above it. The minimum-pool number is measured on one fixture of eleven short executive summaries, so the eight-document floor should be re-read against the pooled-statement count (~71) for corpora of a different document length.
